title: Card and Krueger's 1993 fast-food study reported a rise, not a fall, in New Jersey employment after a minimum-wage increase
summary: Card and Krueger's 1993 fast-food study reported a rise, not a fall, in New Jersey employment after a minimum-wage increase.
body: Card and Krueger's NBER working paper 4509 studies fast-food stores after New Jersey raised its minimum wage on 1 April 1992 from $4.25 to $5.05 an hour, with Pennsylvania stores as a comparison where the minimum did not rise. The paper reports that, relative to stores in Pennsylvania, fast-food restaurants in New Jersey increased employment by 13 percent. The source says: "Relative to stores in Pennsylvania, fast food restaurants in New Jersey increased employment by 13 percent." The paper itself says a competitive model predicts that a higher minimum wage reduces employment, and that studies in the 1970s using aggregate teenage employment rates usually confirmed a negative effect, while some establishment-level studies did not. Thirteen percent is this paper's estimate for this industry and this episode. It is not a universal measurement of minimum-wage effects.

sources.title: Minimum Wages and Employment: A Case Study of the Fast Food Industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, NBER Working Paper 4509
sources.author: David Card and Alan B. Krueger

said_by: David Card and Alan B. Krueger

contested_views.label: This paper's New Jersey–Pennsylvania estimate
contested_views.summary: Relative to Pennsylvania fast-food stores, New Jersey stores increased employment by about 13 percent after the April 1992 rise from $4.25 to $5.05, in the authors' report.
contested_views.status: Card and Krueger, NBER Working Paper 4509, October 1993

contested_views.label: The negative-employment prediction, as this paper describes the earlier literature
contested_views.summary: The paper says the competitive model predicts lower employment, and that 1970s studies of aggregate teenage employment rates usually found a negative effect. It cites Stigler (1946) for the competitive prediction.
contested_views.status: Characterized inside the same working paper. Stigler's text was not re-opened for this card.
